title: AGENT
universal_lens: The AGENT.md protocol defines a discrete-time, multi-agent state-transition system. It enforces mutual exclusion via PID locks, implements fail-closed boundary conditions for covariate injection, and establishes an append-only, causally ordered event bus to prevent temporal leakage in high-frequency predictive environments.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, the covariate-bus acts as a strict Bayesian prior filter. By dropping week=0 season-level aggregates and failing closed on nulls, it prevents look-ahead bias. The SEP bind operator ensures conformal prediction intervals remain valid by strictly isolating exogenous features from target leakage.
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes these primitives for situational reasoning: the watchdog PID acts as a mutex lock preventing concurrent state mutations. The OWNER_GATE and BLOCK states represent hard constraints in the decision graph, ensuring that only verified, non-conflicting edge hypotheses are injected into the live execution engine.

primitives.name: Covariate Bus Fail-Closed Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: - covariate-bus.ts: pure, leak-safe, week=0 dropped, null→fail-closed, weekly_ngs_mean grain, y-axis fields (expectedCompletionPct/avgExpectedYac/expectedRushYards/cpoe/ryoe) absent by construction.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: X_t: Covariate value at time t (dimensionless), t: Discrete week index (integer), D_{t-1}: Historical dataset up to t-1.
primitives.assumptions: Data is strictly causal; future information cannot leak into current state. Week 0 represents undefined seasonal priors.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if t=0 is requested or if the underlying data stream returns a null pointer, triggering a hard drop of the sample.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSI's temporal isolation layer, ensuring feature matrices are strictly lower-triangular relative to the target variable.
layer2.telemetry: Test suite pass rate (e.g., 2870 passed / 2 failed).

primitives.name: SEP Bind Null-Drop Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: - props-hb-adot-sep-bind.ts: binds sepForKickoff into aDOT×SEP samples, drops on null (never 3.0 yards).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: S_bound: Bound sample set, a_i: Average depth of target (yards), s_i: Separation metric (yards).
primitives.assumptions: Missing separation data implies insufficient signal quality to generate a reliable expectation; imputation introduces bias.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks if the upstream provider defaults to an arbitrary constant (e.g., 3.0 yards) instead of returning a true null.

layer2.mapping: Forms the core kernel for GSE's prop-edge detection, strictly coupling spatial metrics without artificial inflation.
layer2.telemetry: Sample rejection rate during binding phase.

primitives.name: Watchdog PID Mutex
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Format ### YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM CT | AGENT | CLEAN|BLOCK|FAKE-EDGE|OWNER_GATE - Who / what - Evidence (PR, HTTP, PID) - Next action (one owner) ## Rules - Do not start a second Hermes if handoff/cheap-overnight/watchdog.pid is live.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: L(p): Lock status (boolean), p: Process ID (integer).
primitives.assumptions: The operating system guarantees unique PIDs for active processes; file system checks are atomic.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Deadlocks if the primary agent crashes without cleaning up the PID file, requiring manual intervention (OWNER_GATE).

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's single-writer constraint, preventing race conditions during parallel edge hypothesis generation.
